scope: Focused read-only review of observer costs and timing boundaries; no protocol changes, tests or measurements.

warmup_complete.measured_quantity: Remaining wait after preceding actions and recorder work, including readiness-observer cost; not total product warmup time since opening.
warmup_complete.observer: loadedPrefix monotonically scans every loaded logical line through isContentLineLoaded. The first unloaded flag can be reread on each 16 ms poll.
warmup_complete.representation_dependency: isContentLineLoaded calls flags[index]; ChunkedList adds bounds checking and a chunk-map lookup. Identical observer code therefore does not imply identical cost.
warmup_complete.initial_ready_case: If all content is already loaded and pendingReads is zero at entry, this phase can largely measure the readiness scan and observer overhead.
warmup_complete.raw_diagnostic: details.loadedPrefixAtFirstCheck shows how much was ready at the first check, not scan duration. No separate scan timer is recorded.
warmup_complete.warning: Do not attribute a warmup_complete difference directly to loading speed or subtract an estimated scan cost from it.

snapshot.fields: requestsStarted, pendingReads, content.length, content/flags runtime types, contentVersion; selects the last nonclosed tracked reader.
snapshot.does_not_do: No content or flag element scan, list copy, loaded-line count, or whole-book snapshot.
snapshot.boundaries: For ordinary book phases, recorder countersBefore/countersAfter call snapshot outside the Stopwatch; the reader wrapper's before/after snapshots are inside it.

durationMs_inside: The action itself, including _wait readiness predicates, 16 ms waits and tester.pump.
Reader before snapshot, SmartText reset, timeline markers, no-content-I/O checks, SmartText takeAndReset and reader after snapshot.
Active profiling work during the action: SmartText counters/classification, timeline instrumentation, RSS timer and delivered frame callbacks.
durationMs_outside: heapBefore and recorder countersBefore; initial RSS read/timer construction.
verifyAction, final RSS read and recorder countersAfter.
The profile 250 ms frame-delivery drain (release uses 1200 ms), heapAfter, JSON journal encoding/writing/flush.
Trace setup/retrieval around recorder.phase, trace serialization/file write and pipeline postprocessing.
timing_boundaries.frames: Engine build/raster/total durations for frames whose build-start wall time is in [startUs,endUs). Preparations before that interval are excluded by attribution. A frame may finish after the Stopwatch stops; its full duration is still reported if delivered during collection. The drain is not added to action latency.
timing_boundaries.layout_paint: Pipeline totals use the narrower reader timeline window: after before-snapshot/SmartText reset, and before takeAndReset/after-snapshot. Only complete LAYOUT/PAINT intervals inside it are included, unioned per thread. They are not additive with latency, repository waits or FrameTiming.
timing_boundaries.repository_reads: durationUs encloses await repository.action; wrapper record construction is outside that individual read timer but can occur inside action latency. The read duration includes queueing, decoding, IPC and scheduling; it is not physical-disk time.
timing_boundaries.memory: Heap/RSS observe the instrumented process, including probe/trace/frame allocations. Heap sampling is outside action latency and does not force GC; it is not isolated retained product memory.

interpretation_limits: Observer costs were not measured separately; no overhead magnitude or correction factor is established.
The warmup scan is a direct representation-dependent observer. Open/jump waitText predicates also read one flag and one content item per poll, rather than scanning the whole book.

SmartText diagnostics can add work proportional to render/HTML activity. Equal instrumentation can amplify different amounts of product work; results remain measurements of the instrumented profile build.
Excluded recorder/trace/heap work still creates gaps between actions during which background loading may advance or be perturbed. Summing phase latencies is not end-to-end elapsed user-flow time.

Frame timings are not instrumentation-free and do not establish physical-GPU/FPS performance. Attribution is by build start, not proof that every part of a frame lies inside the action or that every engine frame was delivered.
